/legal/service-description.title: Service Description | Pren
/legal/service-description.description: Description of Pren’s cloud-based hotel operating system service.
h2: Helping exceptional founders do their best work.
p: Pren is an agentic operating system for hotels that consolidates core hotel software into one system that can complete certain work autonomously. The system includes a property management system (PMS); booking engine; revenue management system (RMS); housekeeping system; payments; point of sale system (POS); meetings, incentives, conferences and exhibitions system (MICE); channel manager; and central reservation system (CRS). The Service is provided as a cloud-based subscription service, accessed via web browser and, where applicable, mobile applications. The specific modules, properties, and usage volumes covered by Customer’s subscription are set out in the applicable Order Form.

2.1. Property Management System (PMS)Reservation management, guest profiles, check-in and check-out, room and rate management, folio management, analytics, and operational reporting.2.2. Booking EngineA booking flow configurator where the Customer can build custom booking pipelines that serve as a direct booking interface for Customer’s website, allowing guests to search availability, book offered rooms and services, and pay online.2.3. Housekeeping SystemRoom status management, task assignment, and housekeeping scheduling. Mobile interface for housekeeping staff to use on the go.2.4. Revenue Management System (RMS)Rate and availability management, including automated pricing recommendations based on demand, occupancy, and market data.2.5. PaymentsProcessing of guest payments through Pren’s integrated payment functionality, subject to the payment terms in the Agreement and the terms of the applicable payment processor. Payment processing may require a separate agreement with, and approval by, the payment processor.2.6. Point of Sale (POS)Sales registration for restaurants, bars, spas, and other outlets, including charge-to-room functionality and fiscal compliance features where required by applicable local law and supported by the Service in the relevant jurisdiction. Includes physical hardware and software.

2.7. MICE (Meetings, Incentives, Conferences, and Exhibitions)Management of group bookings, events, and function spaces, including proposal and banquet event order (BEO) creation, and electronic signature of event agreements.2.8. Channel ManagerDistribution of rates and availability to, and retrieval of reservations from, connected third-party distribution channels (OTAs). Available channels are listed in the Documentation and may be subject to change over time.2.9. MessagesA unified inbox that syncs email and selected OTAs, allowing Customer to send messages and respond to messages.2.10. Agentic FunctionalityCertain workflows within the Service can be executed autonomously or semi-autonomously by the Service’s AI agents, such as answering guest messages, creating or editing bookings, and creating and assigning tasks to staff. Customer can configure the degree of autonomy, including requiring human approval for designated actions. Customer remains responsible for reviewing and supervising agent output as described in Section 5.2.11. Add-onsCertain features may be designated in the Order Form or Documentation as optional add-ons available at additional cost. Features not listed in the Order Form are not included in Customer’s subscription.

The Service is provided as software-as-a-service (SaaS), hosted by Pren or its hosting providers, and accessed over the internet via a supported web browser, or mobile application where applicable. For some functionality, such as POS, peripheral hardware drivers or applications may be required (for example, POS terminals, key card encoders, or printers). Planned maintenance is performed, where reasonably possible, outside peak hours with advance notice for maintenance expected to cause material downtime. Data hosting is described in the Data Processing Agreement.

4.1. Pren provides the following onboarding services for each property, included in the subscription unless otherwise stated in the Order Form: (a) initial configuration of the Service (property setup, room types, rates, taxes, users); (b) migration of reservation and guest data from Customer’s previous system, to the extent such data is made available in a format reasonably usable by Pren; (c) activation of connections to distribution channels and integrations included in the Order Form; and (d) training for Customer’s staff of up to 10 hours delivered remotely. 4.2. Larger implementation projects, custom integrations, on-site training, and migration of data beyond the scope above are provided as professional services under a separate Statement of Work at Pren’s then-current rates, unless otherwise stated in the Order Form. 4.3. Customer is responsible for providing timely access to data, systems, and personnel required for onboarding. Timelines assume Customer meets its responsibilities; delays attributable to Customer may extend the implementation schedule.

Customer is responsible for: (a) maintaining internet connectivity, supported browsers, and any local hardware required to use the Service; (b) the accuracy, legality, and quality of data entered into or migrated to the Service; (c) administering user accounts and ensuring credentials are kept confidential and used only by authorized personnel; (d) configuring the Service, including rates, taxes, policies, and the scope of autonomous agent actions, in accordance with Customer’s business requirements and applicable law; (e) reviewing output generated by the Service, including AI-generated content and autonomous actions, and correcting errors where needed; Customer acknowledges that AI-generated output may contain inaccuracies; (f) compliance with laws applicable to Customer’s operation of its business, including hospitality, tax, fiscal reporting, and guest registration requirements, and consumer and privacy laws in relation to Customer’s guests; and (g) maintaining agreements with third parties whose services Customer uses in connection with the Service, such as OTAs and payment processors.

For the avoidance of doubt, the Service does not include: (a) hardware, including POS terminals, payment terminals, printers, door locks, or key cards, unless expressly stated in the Order Form; (b) third-party services, including OTA listings, payment processing services provided by the payment processor, accounting systems, and door lock systems; Pren provides integrations to certain third-party services but is not responsible for their availability or performance; (c) custom development, custom integrations, or custom reports, unless agreed in a Statement of Work; (d) legal, tax, or revenue management advice; pricing recommendations and compliance features are tools, and decisions based on them remain Customer’s responsibility; (e) telephony, internet access, or on-premise IT infrastructure; (f) recovery of data lost due to actions of Customer or its users beyond restoration from Pren’s standard backup; and (g) forward deployed engineers for onboarding, unless expressly stated in the Order Form.

h2: Helping exceptional founders do their best work.
p: 1.1 The Customer and Pren have entered into the Agreement. This data processing agreement (the “DPA”) supplements the Agreement.
1.2 Within the undertakings arising from the Agreement, Pren will process personal data and other information on behalf of the Customer.
1.3 For that reason, the Parties confirm that this DPA shall regulate the conditions for Pren’s processing of, and access to, personal data on behalf of the Customer.

Unless the circumstances clearly indicate otherwise, definitions or terms used in this document shall be defined as set forth below and any such definition or term which is used in the General Data Protection Regulation and which is not stated below shall be defined as follows from Article 4 of the General Data Protection Regulation. Definitions are also set out in the Agreement.

“Controller” means the natural or legal person, public authority, agency or other body which, alone or jointly with others, determines the purposes and means of the processing of personal data; where the purposes and means of such processing are determined by Union or Member State law, the controller or the specific criteria for its nomination may be provided for by Union or Member State law.

“General Data Protection Regulation” means Regulation 2016/679 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 27 April 2016 on the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data and on the free movement of such data and repealing Directive 95/46/EC.
“Instruction” means the instructions the Customer gives Pren within the scope of this DPA, as further set out in Sub-Appendix 1.
“Other Regulatory Regime” means national laws applicable from time to time to processing of personal data (excluding the General Data Protection Regulation).
“Processor” means a natural or legal person, public authority, agency or another body which processes personal data on behalf of the Controller.

3.1 This DPA consists of this document and the attached instruction. In the event of any contradiction between the documents and the instructions, this document shall prevail, unless otherwise specified or unless another document expressly states otherwise.

3.2 Irrespective of what the Parties have otherwise agreed regarding conflicts, the provisions of this DPA shall take precedence over all other provisions of the Agreement and its appendices in cases where the conflict relates to processing of personal data.
4.1 The Customer is the Controller of the personal data processed in connection with performance and provision of services under the Agreement and its appendices.

4.2 Pren is to be considered as Processor on behalf of the Customer. As a Processor, Pren is responsible for carrying out all processing of personal data on behalf of the Customer in accordance with this DPA, the Instruction, and the General Data Protection Regulation.

4.3 Pren has provided sufficient warranties regarding implementation of appropriate technical and organisational measures in such manner that the processing of personal data fulfils the requirements of the General Data Protection Regulation and Other Regulatory Regime, and to ensure that the rights of the data subjects are protected. The Customer represents and warrants that it has obtained and maintains all consents, authorisations, and other lawful grounds required to permit Pren to process personal data in accordance with this DPA and the Instruction, and that it has fulfilled its obligations to inform the relevant data subjects accordingly.

4.4 Taking into account the nature of the processing, Pren shall, through appropriate technical and organisational measures, assist the Customer, to the extent possible, so that the Customer can fulfil its obligation to respond to requests regarding exercise of the rights of the data subjects in accordance with Chapter III of the General Data Protection Regulation.

4.5 If Pren considers that an Instruction or other instruction or communication from the Customer infringes the General Data Protection Regulation or Other Regulatory Regime, Pren shall promptly notify the Customer, and Pren may suspend performance of the relevant processing until the Customer confirms or amends the instruction in writing, without liability to Pren for any resulting delay.
The Instruction shall, inter alia, state the subject of the processing, the duration, nature and purpose of the processing, the type of personal data, and the categories of data subjects.

This DPA shall apply as from execution of the Agreement and shall remain in force for as long as Pren or any subprocessor retained by Pren processes personal data on behalf of the Customer within the scope of the undertakings arising from this DPA, the Agreement, and appendices.

7.1 Pren, its employees, and other persons carrying out work under Pren’s supervision, and who are given access to personal data by the Customer, may only process such personal data as instructed by the Customer, unless otherwise follows from an obligation under EU or applicable national law.

7.2 Pren shall ensure that its employees and all other persons for whom Pren is responsible and who are authorised to process personal data covered by this DPA undertake to observe confidentiality (unless such person is subject to a relevant and appropriate statutory duty of confidentiality).
8.1 Pren shall take all necessary security measures required in accordance with Article 32 of the General Data Protection Regulation and this DPA.

8.2 In assessing the appropriate level of security in accordance with the clause above, particular account shall be taken of the risks that are presented by the processing, in particular from accidental or unlawful destruction, loss or alteration, or from unauthorised disclosure of, or access to, the personal data transmitted, stored, or otherwise processed.

8.3 Taking into account the type of the processing and the information in possession of Pren, Pren shall assist the Customer in ensuring that the latter’s obligations regarding security can be fulfilled in the manner which follows from Article 32 of the General Data Protection Regulation.

9.1 Taking into account the type of processing and the information reasonably available to Pren, Pren shall provide the Customer with reasonable assistance to enable the Customer to fulfil its obligations under Articles 33–34 of the General Data Protection Regulation. Pren shall be entitled to compensation on a time and material basis for providing such assistance.

9.2 Pren shall notify the Customer without undue delay, and in any event within seventy-two (72) hours, after Pren becomes aware of and has confirmed a personal data breach affecting personal data processed under this DPA.

Pren shall, taking into account the nature of the processing and the information available to Pren, and to the extent reasonably practicable and proportionate to the information available to Pren, assist the Customer in fulfilling its obligations, if any, regarding the performance of a data protection impact assessment and/or prior consultation with a supervisory authority in accordance with Articles 35 and 36 of the General Data Protection Regulation. Pren shall be entitled to compensation on a time and material basis for providing such assistance.

11.1 Pren shall process personal data covered by this DPA only on the Customer’s documented instructions, which shall include: (i) the Instruction set out in Sub-Appendix 1; (ii) any other written instruction issued by the Customer from time to time; and (iii) processing that is reasonably necessary to perform the Agreement, even if not separately documented. Pren may also process personal data (a) where required to do so by EU law or the national law of a Member State to which Pren is subject, in which case Pren shall inform the Customer of that legal requirement before processing unless prohibited on important public interest grounds; or (b) to the extent reasonably necessary for Pren’s own legal, regulatory, security, or compliance purposes, or to establish, exercise, or defend legal claims, in each case consistent with applicable data protection law. If Pren considers that an instruction infringes applicable data protection law, it shall promptly inform the Customer.

11.2 The Instruction may be updated from time to time by written agreement between the Parties. Pren shall not be obliged to comply with an updated Instruction to the extent it would require material changes to Pren’s systems, services, or security measures, unless the Parties agree on appropriate adjustments to timeline, scope, and fees.

12.1 The Customer provides Pren with a general written authorisation to engage subprocessors to carry out processing of personal data under this DPA, subject to the notification and objection mechanism in clause 12.2.

12.2 Pren shall give the Customer at least thirty (30) days’ prior written notice of any intended appointment of a new subprocessor or replacement of an existing subprocessor, identifying the subprocessor and the processing activities concerned. The Customer may object to such appointment or replacement on reasonable, documented data protection grounds by notifying Pren in writing within fifteen (15) days of receipt of such notice. If the Customer does not object within such period, the new subprocessor shall be deemed approved. If the Customer objects on reasonable grounds and the Parties are unable to resolve the objection through good-faith negotiation, the Customer’s sole remedy shall be to terminate the affected services (or the Agreement, to the extent it cannot be performed without the subprocessor) on written notice, without liability to Pren for such termination; provided that such termination right shall not apply to the extent Pren, at its own discretion, decides to either (a) refrain from appointing such new subprocessor, or (b) ensure that such new subprocessor does not process the Customer’s personal data.

12.3 Pren shall ensure that each subprocessor is bound by a written agreement before that subprocessor begins processing personal data in connection with the Agreement. That agreement shall impose data protection obligations on the subprocessor that are no less protective of personal data than those set out in this DPA, to the extent relevant to the processing carried out by that subprocessor.

12.4 The data processing agreement between Pren and any subprocessor shall specifically provide that the subprocessor may only engage a further subprocessor in accordance with the same general authorisation and notice/objection mechanism set out in clauses 12.1 and 12.2 of this DPA.

12.5 Pren shall, from time to time, maintain an updated list of the subprocessors that are retained and have been retained, and the country in which these subprocessors conduct their operations. At the request of the Customer, Pren shall provide the Customer with a copy of the list.

12.6 Pren shall exercise reasonable care in the selection and oversight of any subprocessor and shall remain responsible for ensuring that its subprocessors are contractually bound as required by the Agreement. Neither Party shall be liable to the other for indirect or consequential loss arising out of or in connection with this DPA.

12.7 A Party’s right to seek redress from the other Party under Article 82(5) of the General Data Protection Regulation shall not be restricted by clause 17.1 or by the amount specified in the Agreement’s limitation of liability.

13.1 Upon termination of this DPA, the Customer shall, within fifteen (15) days, provide Pren with written instructions indicating whether it wishes for the personal data to be (i) returned to the Customer, and if so, where and how it shall be returned, or (ii) deleted. Any costs reasonably incurred by Pren in connection with the return of personal data to the Customer, including costs of extraction, formatting, and secure transmission, shall be borne by the Customer. Should the Customer fail to provide such instructions, Pren shall have the right to delete the personal data processed under this DPA, unless otherwise required by national legislation or EU law.

13.2 After termination of this DPA, Pren may not keep any personal data received under this DPA, and as soon as Pren has complied with the clause above, Pren’s right to process or otherwise use the personal data ceases (unless storage of the personal data is required by national legislation or EU law or Pren has a legal basis to process relevant personal data). The Customer is solely responsible for exporting and retaining any personal data it requires for its own purposes prior to any deletion in accordance with this clause 18, and Pren shall have no liability for any loss of data following such deletion.

Pren shall be entitled to amend or supplement this DPA, in whole or in part, provided that such amendment does not materially adversely affect the Customer. Pren shall inform the Customer in writing of any such amendment, and the Customer may object to the amendment by notifying Pren in writing within thirty (30) days of receipt of such notice. If the Customer does not object within such period, the amendment shall be deemed accepted. Any other amendments or supplements to this DPA shall only be applicable if made in writing and signed by authorised representatives of the Parties.
The following document is the Instruction. Definitions used in this Instruction shall have the same meaning as in the Agreement, unless the circumstances clearly indicate otherwise.

15.2 Pren (Processor) As set out in the Agreement.

16.1 Subject matter of the Processing The subject matter of Pren’s Processing of Personal Data on behalf of the Customer is: The Customer’s personal data processed in connection with performance and provision of services under the Agreement.
16.2 Purpose of each Processing The purpose of Pren’s Processing of Personal Data on behalf of the Customer is: To provide the services under the Agreement.

16.3 Categories of Processing The measures carried out by Pren as part of the Processing of Personal Data on behalf of the Customer are: Compute, storage and such other Services as described in the Agreement and in the services and initiated by Customer from time to time.

16.4 Categories of Personal Data Pren is entitled to Process the following categories of Personal Data on behalf of the Customer: All personal data used uploaded to the services under the Agreement by the Customer.

16.5 Categories of sensitive Personal Data Pren is entitled to Process the following categories of sensitive Personal Data on behalf of the Customer: Any sensitive personal data uploaded to the services under the Agreement by the Customer.

16.6 Categories of Data Subjects Pren is entitled to Process Personal Data relating to the following categories of Data Subjects: Any data subjects uploaded to the services under the Agreement by the Customers, such as guests, customers, vendors, and representatives thereof.
Pren will Process Personal Data during the following time period: As between Pren and the Customer, the duration of the data processing under this DPA is determined by Customer.

Pren maintains an information security programme designed to ensure the ongoing confidentiality, integrity, availability, and resilience of processing systems and services. This programme is applied consistently to all personal data processed on behalf of the Customer. On the technical side, Pren applies security measures appropriate to the risk, including: encryption of personal data in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher; encryption at rest using AES-256 with keys managed in AWS Key Management Service, covering databases, object storage, and backups; automated daily encrypted backups of production databases with a defined retention period, and multi-AZ replication of the production database for redundancy; role-based access control through centralised single sign-on with multi-factor authentication enforced for all personnel; least-privilege access to production systems, where standing access is limited to read-only and elevated access is granted on a time-limited, per-need basis; logging and audit trails of access to production systems, with centralised monitoring and automated alerting to on-call personnel; network security measures including web application firewalls and private networking for data stores; infrastructure defined as code and subject to automated security scanning prior to deployment; and segregation of production from non-production environments. On the organisational side, access to personal data is granted strictly on a need-to-know basis, is subject to review, and is promptly revoked when no longer required. All personnel with access to personal data are bound by confidentiality undertakings. Pren maintains a structured incident response process with continuous monitoring, automated alerting, and defined on-call responsibilities. Business continuity and disaster recovery arrangements, including redundant infrastructure and automated encrypted backups, are intended to ensure timely restoration of availability and access to personal data in the event of a physical or technical incident. These measures are reviewed on an ongoing basis and may be updated provided the level of protection is not reduced.
